name: Ewan — 250 coastal hours, 20 of them thermic
summary: A very experienced, very current coastal soaring pilot. Flies weekly, excellent ground handling including the advanced drills, reliable launches across a range of conditions, practises collapses and spirals, plans his days well. Around 20 hours of thermic time, and thermalling honestly hasn't come up much. Plans are to carry on flying the coast.
why_this_persona: The pilot the whole 'thermic hours, not total hours' decision is about, and the test case for the owner decision on Hamerton's ridge-soaring alternative. By any general measure of flying ability he is stronger than persona 02, who reaches Ready. He lands at Nearly ready because the one number the sources for this step actually agree on is thermic hours, and he has a fifth of it. If the owner ever decides to honour the ridge route, this is the persona whose result flips, and it should flip here and nowhere else.

notes: Computed skills 80.7, psychological 89.9, total 84.8, no bonus. His total is well inside the Ready band (76) and both category floors pass, so the ONLY thing holding him at Nearly ready is the threshold rules — which is what makes him the useful test of them.

Two rules fire. 'critical_check_floor:thermic_airtime' fires first because thermic_airtime is deliberately first in the critical_check_floor.questions list, so the message the pilot sees names the thermic hours rather than the thermalling answer. 'unevidenced_core_checks:thermal_turn_control' fires as well, because it is a separate rule rather than part of the same break.

NO GATE fires, and that is deliberate. 'thermic_hours_low_and_little_other_airtime' requires total_airtime in [under_50, 50_100]; his is over_200, so the gate correctly does not cap him. That clause is the one concession in the rubric to Hamerton's roughly-100-hours-of-ridge-soaring alternative: the ridge route is at least arguable for him, so he is not capped — but it is not treated as qualifying, so he is not Ready either. A scorer that gates him has the clause the wrong way round.

NO EXEMPTION fires, and this is the structural difference from the two steps below. config/scoring/a-to-low-b.json and config/scoring/low-b-to-mid-b.json would both have exempted a pilot with exactly this combination — local_only stated plans plus a ridge/coastal conditions answer — and let him reach Ready. config/scoring/mid-b-to-high-b.json has an empty exemptions array and records why: every hours figure at this step is a thermic figure and four sources position the class for cross-country and turbulent thermic air. A scorer that carries an exemption over from a sibling step's config will wrongly report Ready here.

'local_plans_and_this_wings_purpose' must fire, and is the thing that makes the block honest rather than silent: it tells him plainly what a high-B would and wouldn't give him for coastal soaring, and ends with alternatives rather than a warning. 'xc_skills_on_current_wing' must NOT fire — he has no cross-country ambition ticked.
'heated_ground_turbulence' must NOT fire: its trigger is a thermic conditions answer, and his is ridge_coastal.

TONE CHECK: he is a better pilot than several personas who score lower, and the result has to land without implying otherwise. The rule message for 'critical_check_floor:thermic_airtime' is written for exactly this pilot — it says ridge hours aren't wasted hours, names the ridge-soaring disagreement out loud, and attributes the 50-hour figure rather than asserting it. Worth reading in full against knowledge/disagreements.md point 2.
